narrative: The model estimated a 45% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. That is not a certainty, but it is high enough to exceed the bank’s approval cutoff, so your application was denied. The decision was driven mainly by three factors. The strongest was your credit history: you have no credits or all paid, a profile seen in only about 1% of approved applicants, so your repayment record is treated as too unproven. This pushed the decision toward bad risk. The second factor was your checking account balance of 0–200 DM. This modest balance suggests little financial cushion if your income is interrupted, adding to the risk. The third factor, your requested 12-month term, worked in your favour: it is shorter than the approved average of about 19 months, reducing risk. However, it was not enough to offset the first two concerns. To improve future chances, focus on building a documented repayment history, such as a small credit line or secured card paid on time, and keep a stronger balance in your checking account. You could also ask the bank whether a guarantor, co-applicant, or a smaller request would help, and reapply once your credit record and savings position are stronger.
